#grid(
  columns: (colw, colw, colw),
  column-gutter: gutter,
  align: top,

  [
    #sec[Introduction]
    #para[
      Quantifying ecosystem characteristics remains an important step toward data-driven conservation and restoration policy, and multiple data streams are available to this end. Acoustic data have been used in concert with biological sampling information collected for example with trawl nets [1], but there is recent interest in non-lethal eDNA sampling as a tool to complement acoustic surveying, for example by assessment of changes in eDNA profiles that occur with acoustic-sensor-measured movement of organisms [2]. There have additionally been assessment of paired hydroacoustic and eDNA surveys by replicating samples, for example along the depth gradient of pelagic lake habitat [3]. The current study investigates eDNA, purse seine, acoustic and water quality data gathered at three sites in July 2025 as potentially complementary for quantification of ecosystem characteristics.
    ]


    #sec[Methods]
    #para[
      #list(
        [Three sites (Oak Bay, San Juan Islands (Willow Island), and Squamish Harbor) were selected to capture a broad spatial extent around the Salish Sea.],
        [At each site, purse seine captures were conducted using a herring net and began at a depth of between 33.1 meters and 44.3 meters.],
        [Acoustic transects were performed using a BioSonics DTX to capture an area representative of the purse seine catch at each site.],
        [Concurrent eDNA samples were collected at six depths at a central point at each site.],
        [Water quality data were collected at the same central point at each site using an EXO[3?] Multiparameter sonde.]
      )
    ]

    #para[
      #list(
        [Purse seine data is indexed by site, sonde data is indexed by site and depth (layer), acoustic data is 
        indexed by site and depth layer, and eDNA data is indexed by site and discrete depth (layer).],
        [Thus, models that assume independence (e.g., the two-group t-tests, unrestricted-permuatations PERMANOVA) are inappropriate except for the data is aggregated to the site-level.]
      )
    ]
    #v(0.08in)
    #align(center)[#text(size: 18pt, weight: 700)[Map of study area]]
    #image("figures/original-assets/crops/map.png", width: 120%)
    #v(0.08in)
